title: A new challenge notification says 'tap to see it on the leaderboard' but opens the My gym part instead
what: When a gym starts a challenge, members get a pop-up that ends 'Tap to see it on the leaderboard.' The tap opens the Gym tab on its My gym part (membership, timings, check in). The challenge and the leaderboard live in the other part, Ranking, so the member has to find it themselves.
expected: Tapping the challenge pop-up opens the Ranking part of the Gym tab, where the challenge is shown on top.
who: members of a gym that starts a challenge
fix_line: Give the challenge pop-up its own address that opens the Ranking part

title: The same things go by different names on the Gym tab: Ranking or leaderboard, poster or check-in QR
what: The Gym tab's part is called 'Ranking', but its card, the privacy switches, the empty line and the challenge pop-up all call it the leaderboard. The check-in sign at the desk is 'the poster' on the gym-not-found card and the join screen, but 'the gym's check-in QR' on the Check in row. A first-time member can think these are different things.
expected: One name for each thing everywhere: either Ranking or Leaderboard, and either poster or check-in QR.
fix_line: Pick one word for the ranking part and one for the check-in sign and use them everywhere

title: Find my gym asks for a '6-letter code', but gym codes have letters and numbers
what: When finding a gym by number is not open, the member is told to ask for the gym's 6-letter code. Gym codes can hold digits too, and the join box itself says the code has 6 letters and numbers. A member told 'letters' may misread a 0 as an O.
expected: Say '6-character code' or 'the code of 6 letters and numbers', the same as the join box.
who: members without a gym who try Find my gym or phone sign-in
how_often: only while finding by number is closed
fix_line: Use the join box's words for the code in both messages

items.note: All user strings of the 50 files pulled out (746 lines) and read. English only: this area and the member app have no Hinglish, so the Hinglish and Hindi read-aloud parts do not apply. No inside words found (server, sync, session, PR, volume, ForgeAI) except 'server' on test builds only. No banned-word list given beyond the member-words rule in gymIconWords.ts:8.

35 register rows for these files read. 'Only the person you pick sees your question' holds for Ask a trainer: register row P-A7-phone-watch-2-25 marks it GAP using the Message-your-gym path (0096), not the ask path (0053:128-136).
Every greyed button found has its reason in view (out of stock, most already in bag, pick dates, pick a plan, empty message box).
English only. Rows wrap; long names are cut with a trailing ... on one line (leaderboard name, mate name), the platform way; no fixed no-wrap or unshrinkable width found.

No bundled picture file is pointed at in these files: the gym logo comes from the gym, product art and the bell and bag are drawn in code. The notification small icon is set app-wide, outside this area.
No old-brand picture in these files; the ForgeAI name appears only in code comments and ids, never on screen.
One handler: /workout, /shop (opens My gym), /shop/inbox, /shop/ask, the live workout, and any other plain app path.
Every kind lands on a page that exists; only the challenge lands on the wrong part.

items.reason: No save button for changed settings in these files; the greyed send buttons wait for input, not for a change.

items.note: These screens promise no record themselves; the privacy notice they link to says every look is recorded, and the existing findings cover the database's own routes.
